shots: close-up of a small open notebook with neat handwritten work hours beside a pay stub on a break room table, a man's dark hands holding a phone with a calculator, fluorescent light, no readable text

shots.en: Seven thirty. Eight fifteen. Nine forty-five...
shots.fr: Sept heures trente. Huit heures quinze. Neuf heures quarante-cinq...

shots.en: No. No, no, no.
shots.fr: Non. Non, non, non.

shots: a 38 year old West African man from Ivory Coast with dark brown skin, short black hair and a trimmed beard, wearing a gray work jacket over a plaid shirt standing in a warehouse parking lot at dusk holding his phone up for a video call, frustrated face, breath visible in the cold air, parked cars

shots.en: Cheri, you look like somebody stepped on your shoe.
shots.fr: Chéri, tu as la tête de quelqu'un à qui on a marché sur le pied.

shots.en: They are short. Almost two hundred dollars this month. I counted every hour.
shots.fr: Il manque de l'argent. Presque deux cents dollars ce mois-ci. J'ai compté chaque heure.

shots.en: Then do it the right way. Go to the man. Don't fight in the street like a boy. Take an elder.
shots.fr: Alors fais-le comme il faut. Va voir l'homme. Ne te bats pas dans la rue comme un gamin. Prends un ancien avec toi.

shots.en: Papa Jean.
shots.fr: Papa Jean.

shots.en: Papa Jean.
shots.fr: Papa Jean.

shots: a 38 year old West African man from Ivory Coast with dark brown skin, short black hair and a trimmed beard, wearing a gray work jacket over a plaid shirt speaking loudly with his arms open on a warehouse loading dock, three coworkers in work jackets watching him in surprise, a Latino man, a Black woman holding a phone and a white man, morning light, boxes on pallets

shots.en: This man is taking from us. Check your money. Every one of you.
shots.fr: Cet homme nous vole. Vérifiez votre argent. Chacun d'entre vous.

shots.en: Whoa, man...
shots.fr: Hé, doucement...

shots.en: ¿Es verdad?
shots.fr: ¿Es verdad?

shots: the front porch of a modest suburban house on a Sunday afternoon, a 38 year old West African man from Ivory Coast with dark brown skin, short black hair and a trimmed beard, wearing his best navy suit and tie and a 70 year old West African church elder with dark skin and white hair, wearing a dark suit and holding a wooden cane standing respectfully at the door with heads slightly bowed, a 55 year old white American man with short graying hair and a mustache, wearing a flannel shirt in the open doorway looking startled, family dinner visible inside

shots.en: Good afternoon, sir. We will not take long. We come in peace.
shots.fr: Bonjour, monsieur. Nous ne serons pas longs. Nous venons en paix.

shots.en: You came to my house? On a Sunday?
shots.fr: Vous venez chez moi ? Un dimanche ?

shots.en: Where I come from, when there is a matter between two men, you go to the man. You do not write a paper behind his back.
shots.fr: Chez moi, quand il y a une affaire entre deux hommes, on va voir l'homme. On n'écrit pas un papier derrière son dos.

shots.en: Where I come from, you don't call a man a thief in front of his crew. This goes through HR. Monday.
shots.fr: Chez moi, on ne traite pas un homme de voleur devant son équipe. Ça passe par les ressources humaines. Lundi.

shots: a 70 year old West African church elder with dark skin and white hair, wearing a dark suit and holding a wooden cane placing a comforting hand on the shoulder of a 38 year old West African man from Ivory Coast with dark brown skin, short black hair and a trimmed beard, wearing his best navy suit and tie on a front walkway in front of a closed door, autumn afternoon light

shots.en: You did the first part right. Now let God do the rest.
shots.fr: Tu as bien fait la première partie. Maintenant, laisse Dieu faire le reste.

shots: a small office, a 45 year old Haitian-American woman with brown skin and short natural hair, wearing a navy fleece vest and a lanyard laying a handwritten notebook, a printed timesheet and a pay stub on a table, a 38 year old West African man from Ivory Coast with dark brown skin, short black hair and a trimmed beard, wearing a gray work jacket over a plaid shirt and a 55 year old white American man with short graying hair and a mustache, wearing a flannel shirt sitting across from each other listening, daylight from a window, no readable text

shots.en: You two have been using two different scales. Watch.
shots.fr: Vous utilisez deux balances différentes, tous les deux. Regardez.

shots.en: Emmanuel, when you write seven point thirty, you mean seven hours and thirty minutes.
shots.fr: Emmanuel, quand tu écris sept virgule trente, tu veux dire sept heures et trente minutes.

shots.en: Of course.
shots.fr: Bien sûr.

shots.en: Our system reads it as seven point three hours. That's seven hours and eighteen minutes. Every day, you lost twelve minutes.
shots.fr: Notre système le lit comme sept virgule trois heures. Ça fait sept heures et dix-huit minutes. Chaque jour, tu perdais douze minutes.

shots.en: That's... our system?
shots.fr: C'est... notre système ?

shots.en: Our system. It took his numbers and never asked. That part is on us.
shots.fr: Notre système. Il a pris ses chiffres sans jamais demander. Ça, c'est notre faute.

shots: close-up of a 45 year old Haitian-American woman with brown skin and short natural hair, wearing a navy fleece vest and a lanyard pointing at a line on a pay stub on the table while a 38 year old West African man from Ivory Coast with dark brown skin, short black hair and a trimmed beard, wearing a gray work jacket over a plaid shirt listens thoughtfully, office light, no readable text

shots.en: Emmanuel, back home, when they tell you your pay, is that what lands in your hand?
shots.fr: Emmanuel, chez toi, quand on t'annonce ton salaire, c'est ce que tu reçois dans la main ?

shots.en: Yes. The salary is the salary.
shots.fr: Oui. Le salaire, c'est le salaire.

shots.en: Here, they tell you the pay before taxes. Then they take the taxes out. Nobody stole that. It's withholding, for everybody, even Dale.
shots.fr: Ici, on t'annonce le salaire avant impôts. Puis on retire les impôts. Personne n'a volé ça. C'est la retenue à la source, pour tout le monde, même pour Dale.

shots.en: So part of it was true, and part of it was my measure.
shots.fr: Donc une partie était vraie, et une partie venait de ma mesure.

shots.en: A false balance is abomination to the Lord, but a just weight is his delight. Neither of you is a thief. You just weren't weighing with the same weights.
shots.fr: La balance fausse est en horreur à l'Éternel, mais le poids juste lui est agréable. Aucun de vous n'est un voleur. Vous ne pesiez simplement pas avec les mêmes poids.

shots: a 55 year old white American man with short graying hair and a mustache, wearing a flannel shirt and a 38 year old West African man from Ivory Coast with dark brown skin, short black hair and a trimmed beard, wearing a gray work jacket over a plaid shirt shaking hands across an office table, both faces softened, a 70 year old West African church elder with dark skin and white hair, wearing a dark suit and holding a wooden cane smiling in the doorway behind them, warm light

shots.en: We'll pay the missed minutes, all of them, back to your first day. And the timesheet changes this week: an hours box and a minutes box.
shots.fr: On paiera toutes les minutes manquées, depuis ton premier jour. Et la feuille de temps change cette semaine : une case pour les heures, une case pour les minutes.

shots.en: You came to my door like a man, face to face. I treated it like a threat. I'm sorry.
shots.fr: Tu es venu à ma porte comme un homme, face à face. Je l'ai pris comme une menace. Je suis désolé.

shots.en: And I called you a thief in front of your people. In my country an elder would beat me for that. I'm sorry.
shots.fr: Et moi, je t'ai traité de voleur devant tes gens. Chez moi, un ancien m'aurait battu pour ça. Je suis désolé.

shots.en: Not beat. Correct.
shots.fr: Pas battu. Corrigé.

shots: a 38 year old West African man from Ivory Coast with dark brown skin, short black hair and a trimmed beard, wearing a gray work jacket over a plaid shirt talking calmly to his coworkers on a warehouse loading dock in the morning, a Black woman coworker smiling and holding up a pay stub, a 45 year old Haitian-American woman with brown skin and short natural hair, wearing a navy fleece vest and a lanyard standing nearby, forklifts in background

shots.en: Saturday I said the boss steals. I was wrong in how I said it. The machine read us wrong. It's fixed. Check your stubs. If yours is short, it gets paid too.
shots.fr: Samedi, j'ai dit que le patron vole. J'ai eu tort dans ma façon de le dire. La machine nous a mal lus. C'est réparé. Vérifiez vos fiches de paie. S'il vous manque de l'argent, on vous le paiera aussi.

shots.en: Mine said eight point forty-five. I meant eight forty-five.
shots.fr: Moi, j'avais écrit huit virgule quarante-cinq. Je voulais dire huit heures quarante-cinq.

shots.en: Then you're getting a check too.
shots.fr: Alors toi aussi, tu auras un chèque.

shots: a 38 year old West African man from Ivory Coast with dark brown skin, short black hair and a trimmed beard, wearing a gray work jacket over a plaid shirt sitting on the edge of a bed in a small rented room at night smiling at his phone on a video call, a warm lamp, a Bible on the nightstand

shots.en: So? Is he a thief?
shots.fr: Alors ? C'est un voleur ?

shots.en: No. The scale was not false. Only different. Now it is just.
shots.fr: Non. La balance n'était pas fausse. Seulement différente. Maintenant, elle est juste.

shots.en: And you?
shots.fr: Et toi ?

shots.en: I learned something. In this country, you can go to the man. But first, you check the measure.
shots.fr: J'ai appris quelque chose. Dans ce pays, on peut aller voir l'homme. Mais d'abord, on vérifie la mesure.

shots.en: A false balance is abomination to the Lord, but a just weight is his delight. Proverbs eleven, one.
shots.fr: La balance fausse est en horreur à l'Éternel, mais le poids juste lui est agréable. Proverbes onze, verset un.

shots: a 38 year old West African man from Ivory Coast with dark brown skin, short black hair and a trimmed beard, wearing a gray work jacket over a plaid shirt sitting at a small kitchen table in the morning reading his phone with a calm hopeful face, a cup of coffee, a Bible open beside him, no readable text

shots.en: When you're far from home, even a paycheck can feel like a foreign language.
shots.fr: Quand on est loin de chez soi, même une fiche de paie peut ressembler à une langue étrangère.

shots.en: Not sure how something works here? In Community Covenant, tap Ask for Help. A real person from our team writes back the same day, with the Word and a next step.
shots.fr: Vous ne savez pas comment ça marche ici ? Dans Community Covenant, touchez Ask for Help. Une vraie personne de notre équipe vous répond le jour même, avec la Parole et une prochaine étape. L'application est en anglais pour l'instant.

shots.en: Every morning it reads Scripture over you, with gospel music, and walks you into prayer.
shots.fr: Chaque matin, elle vous lit les Écritures, avec de la musique gospel, et vous conduit dans la prière.

shots.en: Get Community Covenant at covenant dot crispusmundo dot com. You are not alone.
shots.fr: Téléchargez Community Covenant sur covenant point crispusmundo point com. Vous n'êtes pas seul.

shots: a hotel ballroom wealth seminar, a 45 year old white American man with very white teeth and gelled hair, wearing a shiny blazer and a headset microphone on stage with arms spread wide, a large screen behind him with a chart, a laughing crowd in rows, a 44 year old Nigerian-born doctor with dark brown skin, short black hair and rimless glasses in blue hospital scrubs under a blazer taking notes in the third row, no readable text

shots.en: Tenants are not people, folks. Tenants are numbers! You buy it, you rent it, you cash it. Let the property manager handle the drama.
You're a professional. Price like one!

shots: a 44 year old Nigerian-born doctor with dark brown skin, short black hair and rimless glasses in a wool coat showing a freshly painted small house with old windows to a 36 year old African American mother with brown skin and her hair in a neat bun, wearing a gray hoodie holding a baby on her hip, autumn afternoon, living room

shots.en: It is a premium property. The rent reflects that.
It's a lot. But the school is right there, and my oldest can walk to practice.
I am a physician. My properties are kept to a high standard.

shots: a cold dark bedroom at 2 in the morning in winter, frost on the inside of the window, five African American children sleeping in winter coats huddled in one bed, a 36 year old African American mother with brown skin and her hair in a neat bun, wearing a gray hoodie in a coat sitting on the edge of the bed on her phone, worried, blue moonlight

shots.en: Doctor Victor, the furnace is out. It's fifty-two degrees in here. My baby...

shots: a 44 year old Nigerian-born doctor with dark brown skin, short black hair and rimless glasses in blue scrubs half asleep in a hospital on-call room holding a phone to his ear, dim light

shots.en: Put on sweaters. Back home we never had heat in our house, and we survived. I am in surgery in the morning.

shots: close-up of a woman's hands holding a smartphone in a cold dark kitchen, her breath visible, a thermostat on the wall behind her, no readable text

shots.en: I need this fixed today. Heat is required here in winter. It's in the housing code for a reason.
Are you threatening me?
I'm telling you my kids are cold.

shots: a 44 year old Nigerian-born doctor with dark brown skin, short black hair and rimless glasses pacing in a modern condo at night, talking to a tablet propped on the counter showing a video call with a small 75 year old Nigerian woman with dark skin wearing a colorful headwrap, warm rain falling behind her

shots.en: She quotes codes at me like I am a criminal. I gave her a beautiful house.
Victor. When you were a boy, why did your father raise our house on blocks?
For the rains. So the floods would not come in.
And when the town made everybody build that way, was that law against your father?
No. It saved us. The year of the big flood, it saved everybody.

shots: warm sepia memory of a small West African town in heavy rain, a modest house raised on concrete blocks above flood water, a father and young son standing dry on the porch, film grain

shots.en: Then their cold law is their flood law. It is not an insult. It is mercy, written down by people who buried children before you came.
You were not raised to let a child sleep cold. Who sold you this idea of tenants?
A man in a ballroom.
Then go back to the house. Not to a ballroom.

shots: a winter morning kitchen, a 44 year old Nigerian-born doctor with dark brown skin, short black hair and rimless glasses in a wool coat standing frozen in the doorway looking at five African American children eating breakfast in their winter coats, a 50 year old Latina HVAC technician with tan skin and her hair in a ponytail, wearing a navy work uniform kneeling at an open furnace in the background

shots.en: Cracked igniter. Filter hasn't been changed since... ever. And these windows are letting the whole winter in.
Fix all of it.
All of it's gonna cost you.
It already did.

shots: a 44 year old Nigerian-born doctor with dark brown skin, short black hair and rimless glasses and a 36 year old African American mother with brown skin and her hair in a neat bun, wearing a gray hoodie sitting across from each other at a kitchen table with mugs, honest conversation, warm light, a baby in a high chair

shots.en: The man who sold me this said tenants are numbers.
We're not numbers. And you're not a bank. You're a neighbor with a key.
I priced it for who I am, not for what this house is. Until the windows are done, take three hundred off.
And after?
After, it will be the house I said it was.

shots: a 12 year old African American boy in a winter coat leaning in a kitchen doorway with a hopeful grin, warm light, his little siblings behind him

shots.en: Can we take our coats off now?

shots: a 44 year old Nigerian-born doctor with dark brown skin, short black hair and rimless glasses standing up from his seat in a hotel ballroom seminar and walking out down the aisle, the speaker on stage blurred in the background, determined face

shots.en: ...and tenants are just numbers!
Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do it. Proverbs three, twenty-seven.

shots: a 44 year old Nigerian-born doctor with dark brown skin, short black hair and rimless glasses smiling softly at his phone in a hospital hallway, the phone screen glowing, no readable text

shots.en: Whether you hold the keys or pay the rent, you're somebody's neighbor.
Type what you're carrying into Ask for Help in Community Covenant. A real person from our team writes back the same day, with the Word and a next step.
Every morning it reads Scripture over you, with gospel music, and walks you into prayer.
Get Community Covenant at covenant dot crispusmundo dot com. You are not alone.

shots: a 28 year old Indian Christian woman with brown skin and long black hair in a loose braid, wearing a simple cotton kurta, no bindi, plain forehead, no red mark in hair parting sitting on her bed at 2 in the morning with a thick Bible open on her lap, a cheap notebook and a highlighter beside her, a small lamp, Indian apartment bedroom

shots.en: I grew up in church. I could quote what the preacher quoted. But one night I realized I had never read it, the whole thing, myself. So I opened to page one.
shots.hi: मैं चर्च में पली-बढ़ी। पादरी जो वचन सुनाते थे, वह मैं भी सुना देती थी। पर एक रात मुझे एहसास हुआ कि मैंने ख़ुद पूरी बाइबल कभी पढ़ी ही नहीं। तो मैंने पहला पन्ना खोला।

shots: extreme close-up of the first page of an old Bible under warm lamp light, a finger resting at the top of the page, shallow depth of field, text too blurry to read

shots.en: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
shots.hi: आदि में परमेश्वर ने आकाश और पृथ्वी की सृष्टि की।

shots: a notebook full of handwritten questions, colorful sticky notes, a highlighter and coffee rings on a wooden desk beside an open Bible, warm night light, handwriting too blurry to read

shots.en: Nobody told me what to think. I just read. In order. Every word.
shots.hi: किसी ने मुझे नहीं बताया कि क्या सोचना है। मैं बस पढ़ती गई। क्रम से। हर शब्द।

shots.en: Why did God accept Abel and not Cain? Where did Cain's wife come from? Some nights I learned. Some nights I argued.
shots.hi: परमेश्वर ने हाबिल की भेंट क्यों स्वीकार की, कैन की क्यों नहीं? कैन की पत्नी कहाँ से आई? कुछ रातें मैंने सीखा। कुछ रातें मैंने बहस की।

shots: a 28 year old Indian Christian woman with brown skin and long black hair in a loose braid, wearing a simple cotton kurta, no bindi, plain forehead, no red mark in hair parting asleep with her head on an open Bible at a desk, a cold cup of chai beside her, rain on the window, early dawn light

shots.en: Months went by. I fell asleep in Leviticus more than once.
shots.hi: महीने बीत गए। लैव्यव्यवस्था पढ़ते-पढ़ते मैं कई बार सो गई।

shots: a 28 year old Indian Christian woman with brown skin and long black hair in a loose braid, wearing a simple cotton kurta, no bindi, plain forehead, no red mark in hair parting sitting on the floor against her bed at night, the Bible open in her lap, looking up toward the ceiling with a frustrated, searching face, lamp light

shots.en: Who did You come to save? Everybody says everybody. Show me. Don't let me just repeat it.
shots.hi: आप किसे बचाने आए थे? सब कहते हैं, सबको। मुझे दिखाइए। मुझे बस रटने मत दीजिए।

shots.en: For years I questioned Jesus. Not to walk away. To actually know Him.
shots.hi: सालों तक मैंने यीशु से सवाल किए। उनसे दूर जाने के लिए नहीं। उन्हें सच में जानने के लिए।

shots: warm sepia memory of a small Indian kitchen long ago, a 75 year old Indian Christian grandmother with gray hair in a bun, wearing a white cotton sari, no bindi, plain forehead, no red mark in hair parting wiping her hands on her sari and smiling gently at a young girl, steel pots, morning light, film grain

shots.en: Baby, don't be scared of questions. Test the spirits. A true God can stand up to a true question.
shots.hi: बेटा, सवालों से मत डरना। आत्माओं को परखो। सच्चा परमेश्वर सच्चे सवाल के आगे टिक सकता है।

shots: a 28 year old Indian Christian woman with brown skin and long black hair in a loose braid, wearing a simple cotton kurta, no bindi, plain forehead, no red mark in hair parting at her desk at night underlining a verse in her Bible with a pencil, pausing with a quiet amazed look, simple lamp light, no beams of light

shots.en: And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart.
shots.hi: तुम मुझे ढूँढ़ोगे और पाओगे भी, क्योंकि तुम अपने सम्पूर्ण मन से मुझे ढूँढ़ोगे।

shots.en: It wasn't a feeling. It was more like finally meeting someone I had only heard about. I had read my way to Him.
shots.hi: यह कोई एहसास नहीं था। यह ऐसा था जैसे आख़िरकार उस व्यक्ति से मिलना, जिसके बारे में मैंने सिर्फ़ सुना था। पढ़ते-पढ़ते मैं उन तक पहुँच गई थी।

shots: a 38 year old Indian Christian woman with brown skin and black hair in a low bun, wearing a simple cotton kurta, no bindi, plain forehead, no red mark in hair parting leading a small Bible study at her kitchen table with four women of different ages, a wall behind them covered in colorful sticky notes, open Bibles and cups of chai, warm evening light, no readable text

shots.en: Ask anything. If the Word is true, it can handle it.
shots.hi: कुछ भी पूछिए। अगर वचन सच्चा है, तो वह हर सवाल सह सकता है।

shots.en: I still have questions. But they're mine now. And so is my faith.
shots.hi: मेरे सवाल अब भी हैं। पर अब वे मेरे अपने हैं। और मेरा विश्वास भी।

shots.en: They searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. Acts seventeen, eleven.
shots.hi: वे प्रतिदिन पवित्र शास्त्रों में ढूँढ़ते रहे कि ये बातें ऐसी ही हैं कि नहीं। प्रेरितों के काम सत्रह, ग्यारह।

shots: a 38 year old Indian Christian woman with brown skin and black hair in a low bun, wearing a simple cotton kurta, no bindi, plain forehead, no red mark in hair parting on a balcony at sunrise holding a phone in one hand and a Bible in the other, peaceful smile, city rooftops behind her, no readable text

shots.en: Want to read the whole Bible for yourself?
shots.hi: क्या आप पूरी बाइबल ख़ुद पढ़ना चाहते हैं?

shots.en: Community Covenant reads Scripture over you every morning, and walks you through it one chapter at a time.
shots.hi: कम्युनिटी कोवेनेंट हर सुबह आपको वचन पढ़कर सुनाता है, और एक-एक अध्याय करके आपको आगे ले चलता है।

shots.en: Have a hard question? Type it into Ask for Help. A real person from our team writes back the same day.
shots.hi: कोई कठिन सवाल है? उसे Ask for Help में लिखिए। हमारी टीम का कोई व्यक्ति उसी दिन जवाब देगा। ऐप अभी अंग्रेज़ी में है।

shots.en: Get Community Covenant at covenant dot crispusmundo dot com. You are not alone.
shots.hi: कम्युनिटी कोवेनेंट डाउनलोड कीजिए: covenant डॉट crispusmundo डॉट com. आप अकेले नहीं हैं।

shots: a driveway at 4 in the morning in the 1990s, a packed wood-paneled station wagon with coolers and a garment bag of white dresses, a 55 year old African American church mother with brown skin wearing a large white church hat and a white dress wearing a sun hat holding the car door open for a 9 year old African American girl with brown skin and her hair in two puffs with colorful barrettes in pajamas and a jacket, porch light, dark sky

shots.en: Every year, Cousin Lorraine drove from the Great Lakes all the way down to the Delta for Holy Convocation. And every year, she took one child. That year it was me.
Get in, baby. And don't touch that chicken till we cross the state line.

shots: inside an old station wagon on a highway at sunrise, a 55 year old African American church mother with brown skin wearing a large white church hat and a white dress driving and singing joyfully, a 62 year old African American man with gray hair and glasses wearing a cardigan asleep in the passenger seat, a 9 year old African American girl with brown skin and her hair in two puffs with colorful barrettes in the back seat pressing her face to the window, foil-wrapped food on the seat

shots.en: Why do we have to go so far for church? We have church at home.
Because sometimes God wants to see if you'll travel for Him like you'd travel for a party.

shots: a roadside rest stop picnic table in the South in the afternoon, a 55 year old African American church mother with brown skin wearing a large white church hat and a white dress spreading a checkered tablecloth with fried chicken in foil, white bread and pound cake, a 9 year old African American girl with brown skin and her hair in two puffs with colorful barrettes pointing at something off to the side, a 62 year old African American man with gray hair and glasses wearing a cardigan eating

shots.en: Cousin Lorraine, what did that sign used to say?

shots: an old rusted metal sign on a post at a roadside diner, its words painted over and peeling, weeds around the post, afternoon light, no readable text

shots.en: It used to say we couldn't eat inside. So we packed our food and ate out here. And we still sang.
They could take the dining room. They couldn't take the song.

shots: a 55 year old African American church mother with brown skin wearing a large white church hat and a white dress humming with her eyes closed at a picnic table, a 62 year old African American man with gray hair and glasses wearing a cardigan singing beside her, a 9 year old African American girl with brown skin and her hair in two puffs with colorful barrettes watching them in wonder, golden afternoon light

shots.en: That's when I understood the chicken wasn't just chicken.

shots: a huge church convocation hall at night filled with thousands of African American worshippers dressed all in white, church mothers in large white hats, a choir in robes, an organ, tambourines, hands raised, joyful tears

shots.en: Everybody's crying and smiling at the same time.
That's called the Holy Ghost, baby. Hold my purse.

shots: a 9 year old African American girl with brown skin and her hair in two puffs with colorful barrettes looking scared and small in a crowd of adults dressed in white after a church service, an older African American usher in white gloves kneeling down to her eye level kindly

shots.en: Whose baby are you?
Lorraine's.
Which Lorraine? There's three hundred.

shots: a 55 year old African American church mother with brown skin wearing a large white church hat and a white dress in her big white hat calling out loudly above a crowd of worshippers in white, one hand raised, relieved and stern at once

shots.en: Toni Marie!
Oh. That Lorraine.

shots: night at a small gas station, inside the parked station wagon a 9 year old African American girl with brown skin and her hair in two puffs with colorful barrettes asleep on the shoulder of a 55 year old African American church mother with brown skin wearing a large white church hat and a white dress, a 62 year old African American man with gray hair and glasses wearing a cardigan at the wheel, neon light through the window

shots.en: She asked me what the sign said.
What'd you tell her?
The truth. And the song.

shots: present day driveway at 4 in the morning, a 42 year old African American woman with brown skin and shoulder length locs loading a modern car, a young niece buckled in the back seat, foil-wrapped chicken on the front seat, porch light

shots.en: Cousin Lorraine went home to glory a few years back. But I still make the drive. Every year, one child.
Because faith isn't just what they teach you in church. It's what they teach you on the way.
And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou walkest by the way. Deuteronomy six, seven.

shots: a 42 year old African American woman with brown skin and shoulder length locs and her young niece sitting together at a kitchen table looking at a phone and smiling, a Bible and a plate of pound cake on the table, morning light, no readable text

shots.en: Who taught you faith on the way?
Community Covenant reads Scripture over you every morning, with gospel music, and walks you into prayer.
Link your family with one family code. Cheer each other on, and share what God is doing.
Get Community Covenant at covenant dot crispusmundo dot com. You are not alone.
